knownIssues: ComfyUI-llama-cpp_vlm (node types llama_cpp_model_loader / llama_cpp_parameters / llama_cpp_instruct_adv) is a llama.cpp LLM/VLM node that delegates to llama-cpp-python. It is device-agnostic: it only passes n_gpu_layers to llama.cpp, so the runtime device is decided entirely by the installed llama-cpp-python binary's compiled backend.

The node's requirements.txt pins CUDA (+cu128) and Metal wheels only -- there is NO Intel XPU/SYCL wheel. On this Intel XPU/CPU environment the installed binary is CPU-only (only libggml-cpu.so; no libggml-cuda.so / libggml-sycl.so), so n_gpu_layers=-1 is a no-op and the VLM runs on CPU. This is intentional and correct here: CPU inference uses host RAM, NOT the 30 GB XPU VRAM, leaving the XPU free for the fp8 diffusion model.

This node is auto-provisioned by the migration agent's known-custom-node registry (src/server/knownCustomNodes.ts): it is source-known at Step 00, auto-cloned at Step 01, and its GGUF + mmproj weights route to models/LLM/ (NOT text_encoders). It must therefore NOT be treated as source-unknown or as a CUDA-only blocker in Step 02 feasibility -- do not open an ask_user gate for it.
For heavy fp8 diffusion pipelines, step06_prompt_validation.py already sets force_offload=True on llama_cpp* nodes so the ~14 GB VLM is freed after producing conditioning; keep that policy.

workarounds.action: No node change needed. Ensure a CPU-built llama-cpp-python is installed into the shared XPU venv via bash /nfs_share/bin/with-shared-venv-lock.sh <venv_python> install <cpu-wheel>; do NOT pip install -r the node's requirements.txt (it pins CUDA wheels). Place the model .gguf and the mmproj .gguf under models/LLM/.
workarounds.rationale: The node works out of the box once a portable CPU llama-cpp-python is present and the GGUF/mmproj live in models/LLM/; the only failure modes are (a) installing the CUDA requirements.txt, or (b) the models landing in text_encoders where the loader cannot find them -- both are handled automatically by the registry + Step 05 policy.
workarounds.tradeoff: CPU inference for the VLM description stage is slower than a GPU build, but it runs once per generation and keeps the XPU VRAM free for the fp8 diffusion model. XPU acceleration would require a SYCL-built llama-cpp-python (no ready wheel) and would compete for XPU VRAM.
